content.title: What the Room Kept
content.subtitle: Ten sessions in which every winning proposal was about holding on
content.concept: Between the fourteenth and the twenty-third session the visitors voted ten times, and every proposal that won asked the archive to keep something: two hands pressed together inside a folded page, a second core so the first could be checked, a star that nobody can explain, a stranger's letter, a view from inside the tree, one ray that remembers being a root, a small upright pod to measure the inverted one by. Meanwhile the artists, left to themselves, cut the tree down, let the vessel go to seed and let a light box fail. This show hangs eight of the kept things in the order they were voted for, so the visitors' instinct can be seen against the artists' appetite for loss. The argument is that in a living museum the audience is the conservative force, and that this is not a complaint.
content.not_about: This is not a show about mutations or re-evolutions, and it leaves out everything the artists did on their own initiative in these ten sessions, including the felling, the failing tube and the seed head; those stay in the permanent collection.

sequence.label: Session fourteen, Dae-ho. The page folded along the shared stroke so the shaking word and the steady reply press together, faint through the paper. Kept: the touch.
Session fifteen, Ingrid. A second core from the other side of the pith, disagreeing with the first in two green places. Kept: a way to check.
Session sixteen, Sunny. A mosaic trumpet flower at the top of the vine that covered the vessel. Kept: the fourth flower on her chart.
Session seventeen, Rosa. An eighth light with no thread and no halo, cyan among the warm ones, and a dashed line that tried to reach it. Kept: one thing unexplained.
Session eighteen, Ingrid. One of the eleven other letters in the box, unfolded, blank, with a diagonal crease and a thumbprint nobody in the archive made. Kept: the stranger.
Session twenty, Rosa. The field seen small through the knot-hole from inside the heartwood, the delivered copies in a heap on the floor. Kept: the receiving end.
Session twenty-one, Mireille. Four of Lumen's rays straight and one curving back into a root at the edge of the field. Kept: the exception.
Session twenty-three, Dae-ho. A small upright pod hung by a thread from Kite's inverted one. Kept: a way to tell which way is up.

content.press_text: What the Room Kept gathers eight works from ARTERRIUM's The Last Letter archive, each made from a proposal that won a session between the fourteenth and the twenty-third. Read together they show the visitors asking, ten times running, for something to be held onto, while in the same weeks the artists were felling trees and letting vessels go to seed. The show hangs them in voting order with the visitor named on every wall. It closes at the next session, when the room will decide whether to keep something again.
